headline: Worldwide chip sales have passed one trillion dollars in the first eight months of 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association has announced.
score_reason: Curator score 6 lowered by 1: the figures were released on 5 Oct 2026, before the 10 Oct start of today's window.
importance_line: The announcement shows AI-driven demand has taken the chip industry past a trillion dollars in eight months, which matters to chipmakers and to the companies and households that buy their products, but it is an industry-body total that says nothing by itself about prices or profits.
summary: The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA), the main US chip-industry group, said on 5 Oct 2026 that global chip sales reached $159.7 billion in August, up 8% on July and 144.3% on a year earlier, and that sales for the year so far have passed $1 trillion for the first time. The figures are compiled with the independent WSTS statistics body as three-month moving averages, and SIA expects sales above $1.6 trillion for the full year 2026.
notes: Pool link (BusinessToday Malaysia) was blocked (HTTP 403); entry written from the SIA press release (original) and Evertiq. The BusinessToday headline figures (US$957 billion, 103%) differ from SIA's and are not used. Announced 5 Oct 2026, so older than today's window.
